claim: Airinemes are long, thin cellular protrusions extending tens to hundreds of micrometers in zebrafish.
source: However, recently, an alternative cell–cell communication mechanism has been revealed to be long, thin cellular protrusions extending tens to hundreds of micrometers (Eom, 2020; Yamashita et al., 2018; Caviglia and Ober, 2018; Sanders et al., 2013; Bressloff and Kim, 2019; Inaba et al., 2015). These include cytonemes (Kornberg and Roy, 2014), tunneling nanotubes (Zurzolo, 2021), tenocyte projections (Subramanian et al., 2018), and airinemes in zebrafish (Volkening and Sandstede, 2018; Volkening, 2020; Eom and Parichy, 2017; Eom et al., 2015), shown in Figure 1A.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work and reference to Figure 1A showing airinemes.

claim: Airinemes are produced by xanthoblasts (undifferentiated yellow pigment cells).
source: Airinemes are produced by xanthoblasts (undifferentiated yellow pigment cells) and play a role in the spatial organization of pigment cells that produce the patterns on zebrafish skin (Eom et al., 2015; Eom and Parichy, 2017; Eom, 2020; Volkening and Sandstede, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Airinemes play a role in the spatial organization of pigment cells that produce patterns on zebrafish skin.
source: Airinemes are produced by xanthoblasts (undifferentiated yellow pigment cells) and play a role in the spatial organization of pigment cells that produce the patterns on zebrafish skin (Eom et al., 2015; Eom and Parichy, 2017; Eom, 2020; Volkening and Sandstede, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Macrophages drag protruding airinemes from xanthoblasts as they migrate around the tissue.
source: Macrophages recognize a signal on xanthoblasts and begin dragging a protruding airineme from the xanthoblast as they migrate around the tissue, with the airineme trailing behind them.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript describing the mechanism.

claim: Airineme lengths have a maximum, regardless of whether they reach their target.
source: Airineme lengths have a maximum, regardless of whether they reach their target.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: The airineme tip contains the Delta-C ligand, which activates Notch signaling in the target cell.
source: The airineme tip contains the Delta-C ligand, which activates Notch signaling in the target cell.
evidence: Direct statement about molecular composition and function.

claim: If no target cell is found by the maximum airineme length, the macrophage and airineme disconnect, and the airineme retracts.
source: If no target cell is found by the maximum length, the macrophage and airineme disconnect, and the airineme retracts.
evidence: Direct statement describing the outcome of unsuccessful search.

claim: There is no experimental evidence that the airineme search process responds to any directional cues.
source: In contrast, macrophages pulling airinemes during development are not triggered by tissue damage or infections in zebrafish skin (Eom et al., 2015), and there is no experimental evidence that the airineme search process responds to any directional cues.
evidence: Explicit statement about lack of evidence for directional cues, with citation.

claim: Airinemes extend with constant velocity v = 4.5 μm/min.
source: This allows us to consider only the fully extended airineme and infer the dynamics, assuming airinemes extend with constant velocity v = 4.5 μm/min (Eom et al., 2015).
evidence: Velocity value cited from prior work (Eom et al., 2015).

claim: A simple random walk model is rejected for describing airineme motion.
source: We therefore reject the simple random walk description.
evidence: Conclusion based on MSD analysis showing non-linear behavior.

claim: Levy-type models are not consistent with airineme motion.
source: We thus conclude that the process is not consistent with Levy-type models.
evidence: Conclusion based on CCDF analysis showing exponents greater than 3 and continued downward curvature.

claim: For two time interval choices (10 min and 20 min), the best-fit CCDF exponents are greater than 3.
source: For two time interval choices, shown in Figure 2B, the best-fit CCDF exponents are greater than 3 (for 10 min, exponent is 3.81 with 90% CI in [3.68,3.95]; for 20 min, exponent is 4.40 with 90% CI in [4.18,4.61]).
evidence: Statistical fits to experimental data with confidence intervals.

claim: Airineme shape is most consistent with a finite-length persistent random walk (PRW) model.
source: We find that airineme shape is most consistent with a finite-length PRW model, and that the parameters of this model exhibit an optimum for minimizing the probability of finding a target (or, equivalently, the mean number of attempts).
evidence: Conclusion from comparison of experimental data with multiple models.

claim: The assumption of maximum length 250 μm yields a final length distribution consistent with observed distribution.
source: This assumption yields a final length distribution (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) consistent with the observed distribution (Eom et al., 2015).
evidence: Comparison of model predictions with experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Airinemes operate independently with no evidence of communication between them during search.
source: We also assume that airinemes operate independently as there is no evidence of airinemes communicating with each other during the search process.
evidence: Assumption based on lack of experimental evidence for inter-airineme communication.

claim: Airinemes are generated at approximately 0.15 airinemes per cell per hour.
source: Furthermore, airinemes are generated at approximately 0.15 airinemes per cell per hour.
evidence: Quantitative measurement of airineme generation rate.

claim: Airineme tips appear unrestricted in their motion on the 2D surface, passing over or under other cells unimpeded.
source: Also, while the tissue surface is crowded, the airineme tips (which are transported by macrophages; Eom et al., 2015) appear unrestricted in their motion on the 2D surface, passing over or under other cells unimpeded (Eom and Parichy, 2017).
evidence: Observation from live-cell imaging cited from prior work.

claim: There exists an optimal angular diffusion coefficient that maximizes the chance to contact the target cell.
source: We find that there exists an optimal angular diffusion coefficient that maximizes the chance to contact the target cell.
evidence: Result from simulations shown in Figure 3.

claim: The optimal value of angular diffusion balances between ballistic and diffusion-like search.
source: The optimal value balances between ballistic and diffusion-like search.
evidence: Conclusion from simulation results and theoretical analysis.

claim: If the target cell is small or close, a diffusion-like search process is favored.
source: Thus, if the target cell is small or close, a diffusion-like search process is favored, but if the target cell is far or large, then a ballistic search is favored.
evidence: Inference from simulation results analyzing different target parameters.

claim: If the target cell is far or large, a ballistic search is favored.
source: Thus, if the target cell is small or close, a diffusion-like search process is favored, but if the target cell is far or large, then a ballistic search is favored.
evidence: Inference from simulation results analyzing different target parameters.

claim: The experimentally observed angular diffusion value matches the simulated optimal angular diffusion value for biologically relevant parameters.
source: Surprisingly, as shown in Figure 4B, this value matches our simulated optimal angular diffusion value for the biologically relevant parameter values.
evidence: Comparison of experimental measurement with simulation predictions shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The observed airineme parameters lead to a wide distribution of contact angles compared to both ballistic or diffusion-like airinemes.
source: Interestingly, we find that the observed airineme parameters lead to a wide distribution of contact angles compared to both ballistic or diffusion-like airinemes.
evidence: Result from analysis of contact angle distributions shown in Figure 5B.

claim: For very straight airinemes, allowed contact locations are restricted to a narrow range, resulting in high directional information.
source: For very straight airinemes, the allowed contact locations are restricted to a narrow range (a straight airineme can never hit the target's far side), resulting in high directional information.
evidence: Explanation of directional information results based on geometric constraints.

claim: In the case of zebrafish airinemes, there is no evidence that the shape sacrifices optimal search to achieve increased directional signaling.
source: In other words, in the case of zebrafish airinemes, there is no evidence that the shape of these protrusions sacrifices the goal of optimal search in order to achieve increased directional signaling.
evidence: Conclusion from analysis of trade-off between search and directional information.

claim: Airinemes have suboptical width, which delayed their discovery and characterization.
source: One of the difficulties delaying their discovery and characterization is their thin, suboptical width, and the fact that they only form at specific stages of development (Eom, 2020; Yamashita et al., 2018; Caviglia and Ober, 2018).
evidence: Statement about technical challenges with citations.

claim: Airinemes only form at specific stages of development.
source: One of the difficulties delaying their discovery and characterization is their thin, suboptical width, and the fact that they only form at specific stages of development (Eom, 2020; Yamashita et al., 2018; Caviglia and Ober, 2018).
evidence: Statement about developmental timing with citations.

claim: The airineme MSD fits the prediction of the PRW model up to time point around 15 min.
source: The airineme MSD fits the prediction of the PRW model, in Equation 5, up to time point around 15 min.
evidence: Comparison of experimental MSD with theoretical PRW prediction.

claim: Different cellular protrusions may have shapes optimized for different functions.
source: This raises an intriguing possibility that different protrusions have a shape optimized for different functions.
evidence: Speculation based on observed differences in protrusion morphology.

claim: Some tunneling nanotubes in cancer cells are straight compared to airinemes.
source: For example, some tunneling nanotubes in cancer cells (Parker et al., 2017) are straight compared to airinemes.
evidence: Comparison with other cellular protrusions cited from literature.

claim: Nanotubes in PC12 cells serve as conduits for organelles.
source: For example, nanotubes in PC12 cells serve as conduits for organelles (Wang and Gerdes, 2015).
evidence: Function of nanotubes cited from literature.

claim: The finite PRW process is mathematically equivalent to the worm-like chain model.
source: Mathematically, the finite PRW process is equivalent to the worm-like chain model, for which exact formula have been derived for the tip location (Spakowitz and Wang, 2005; Mehraeen et al., 2008).
evidence: Mathematical equivalence stated with citations to theoretical work.

claim: The contact probability per airineme sets an upper bound on the ability of cells to communicate via this modality.
source: Our results provide a contact probability per airineme, setting an upper bound on the ability of cells to communicate via this modality, which is itself a function of cell density (related to dtarg in our notation).
evidence: Inference about implications of results for cell communication.

claim: Variants of the PRW model have been found to describe cell migration.
source: Variants of the PRW model have been found to describe cell migration (Harrison and Baker, 2018; Weavers et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement about model applications with citations.

claim: A related PRW model was found to accurately describe macrophages in zebrafish.
source: Specifically, a related model was found to accurately describe macrophages in zebrafish (Jones et al., 2015).
evidence: Citation to prior work on macrophage modeling.

claim: Macrophages in zebrafish demonstrate a mix of directional persistence and randomness.
source: Two observations from Jones et al., 2015 are particularly relevant to our work: that macrophages in zebrafish demonstrate a mix of directional persistence and randomness, and that their migration patterns adapt to circumstance (specifically, in their case, distance to wound and time since wounding).
evidence: Summary of findings from cited work (Jones et al., 2015).

claim: Macrophage migration patterns adapt to circumstance such as distance to wound and time since wounding.
source: Two observations from Jones et al., 2015 are particularly relevant to our work: that macrophages in zebrafish demonstrate a mix of directional persistence and randomness, and that their migration patterns adapt to circumstance (specifically, in their case, distance to wound and time since wounding).
evidence: Summary of findings from cited work (Jones et al., 2015).

claim: The variability in both experimental and simulated airineme length distributions is of similar magnitude.
source: Note that the variability in both experimental and simulated distributions is of similar magnitude, suggesting that the randomness in observed airineme length arises from the randomness in target cell placement.
evidence: Comparison of experimental and simulation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The randomness in observed airineme length arises from the randomness in target cell placement.
source: Note that the variability in both experimental and simulated distributions is of similar magnitude, suggesting that the randomness in observed airineme length arises from the randomness in target cell placement.
evidence: Inference from comparison of experimental and simulation variability.

claim: The difference between time-series tip location curvature and final state curvature is on average 0.7%.
source: We computed root mean squared curvature of both the time-series tip location and of just the final state for the airinemes shown here. These two methods yield a difference, on average, of 0.7%.
evidence: Quantitative comparison stated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: The results of the isotropy test are insensitive to the cutoff length.
source: The results of this test are insensitive to the cutoff length (see Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Statement about robustness of statistical test with reference to source data.

claim: Contact is defined as the event in which the tip of the growing airineme intersects with the target.
source: Specifically, contact is defined as the event in which the tip of the growing airineme intersects with the target.
evidence: Definition of contact used in simulations.

claim: In simulations, contact is assumed to have occurred when the airineme tip reaches within a distance rtarg of the center of the target cell.
source: In simulations, we assume contact has occurred when the airineme tip reaches within a distance rtarg of the center of the target cell.
evidence: Operational definition used in computational model.

claim: The mechanism by which contact is detected is unknown.
source: However, as discussed above, the mechanism by which contact is detected is unknown, and it could be that the airineme tip has a large effective spatial extent that includes some or all of the macrophage.
evidence: Statement about limitation of current knowledge.

claim: The search process is finite-length and would not always eventually find the target in two dimensions.
source: Note again the search process is finite-length (otherwise in two dimensions would always eventually find the target).
evidence: Statement about mathematical property of finite vs infinite search.

claim: To maximize contact probability, variance of contact angle should be maximal.
source: Heuristically, this is because the two objectives prefer opposite variances. To maximize contact probability, variance should be maximal, taking full advantage of the surface of the target.
evidence: Heuristic explanation of trade-off mechanism.

claim: To maximize directional information, the variance of contact angle should be minimized.
source: On the other hand, to maximize directional information, the variance of contact angle should be minimized.
evidence: Heuristic explanation of trade-off mechanism.

claim: At intermediate cell-to-cell distances, the parametric curve forms a loop offering a concave-down region with a Pareto optimum.
source: At these intermediate dtarg values, the loop offers a concave-down region with a Pareto optimum.
evidence: Description of parametric curve behavior shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The mathematical characterization of long-range cellular projections will become increasingly valuable as they continue to be discovered.
source: As long-range cellular projections like airinemes continue to be discovered in multicellular systems, their mathematical characterization will become increasingly valuable, mirroring the mathematical characterization of diffusion-mediated cell–cell signals.
evidence: Statement about future importance of this type of research.

claim: The results have implications for macrophage cell motility relevant in wound healing and infection.
source: Since airineme tip motion is driven by macrophages, our results have implications for macrophage cell motility, which is relevant in other macrophage-dependent processes like wound healing and infection (Sun et al., 2019; Achouri et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement about broader implications with citations.

claim: Efficient transport of signaling molecules after contact might prefer shorter protrusion length and favor straight morphologies.
source: Besides search success probability and directional information, one obvious candidate for optimization is the efficient transport of signaling molecules after contact has been established (Bressloff and Kim, 2018; Kim and Bressloff, 2018). This might prefer shorter protrusion length, and therefore favor straight morphologies.
evidence: Speculation about alternative optimization objectives with citations.

claim: There is an opportunity to find analytic expressions for the contact probabilities.
source: There is an opportunity to find analytic (asymptotic or exact) expressions for the contact probabilities, which would obviate the need for stochastic simulation.
evidence: Statement about future mathematical work.

claim: The contact probability per airineme is a function of cell density.
source: Our results provide a contact probability per airineme, setting an upper bound on the ability of cells to communicate via this modality, which is itself a function of cell density (related to dtarg in our notation).
evidence: Statement about relationship between contact probability and cell density.

claim: The results may inform future pattern formation models.
source: Thus, our results may inform future pattern formation models.
evidence: Statement about potential application of results.

claim: Pattern formation models may provide information about the distribution of target cells which may affect search efficiencies.
source: In the reciprocal direction, these models may provide information about the distribution of target cells, which may significantly affect search efficiencies.
evidence: Statement about reciprocal relationship between models.

claim: Time-lapse images were acquired at 5 min intervals for 12 hr at ×40 magnification on a Leica SP8 confocal microscope.
source: Time-lapse images, acquired at 5 min intervals for 12 hr, and static images were taken at ×40 (water-emulsion objective) on a Leica SP8 confocal microscope with resonant scanner.
evidence: Description of imaging methodology.

claim: Zebrafish larvae of 7.5 SSL were staged prior to explant preparation for ex vivo imaging.
source: Zebrafish larvae of 7.5 SSL were staged following Parichy et al., 2009 prior to explant preparation for ex vivo imaging of pigment cells in their native tissue environment as described by Budi et al., 2011 and Eom et al., 2012.
evidence: Description of experimental methodology with citations.

claim: Model convolution was used to estimate uncertainty in the analysis method.
source: In order to estimate uncertainty in our analysis method, we used model convolution (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Gardner et al., 2010).
evidence: Description of uncertainty quantification method with citation.

claim: Independent analyses by five people were performed on both simulated data and experimental data.
source: Since there is a manual step in this analysis pipeline, independent analyses by five people were performed on both simulated data and experimental data.
evidence: Description of validation approach for manual analysis.

claim: Fisher information can be intuitively understood as the inverse of variance for Gaussian distributions.
source: This quantity can be intuitively understood by noting that, for Gaussian distributions, Fisher information is the inverse of the variance. So, high variance implies low information and low variance implies high information.
evidence: Explanation of Fisher information concept.

claim: A target cell that receives almost no airinemes will score low in directional information using the modified Fisher information metric.
source: With this modification, a target cell that receives almost no airinemes will score low in directional information.
evidence: Explanation of rationale for modified Fisher information.

claim: The extracted data and analysis routines are available openly at a GitHub repository.
source: The extracted data and analysis routines are available openly at: https://github.com/sohyeonparkgithub/Airineme-optimal-target-search, (copy archived at swh:1:rev:366ad6e1e3e5061c0cf395c8e3be784872903922; Park, 2021).
evidence: Statement about data and code availability.

claim: Adult zebrafish were maintained at 28.5°C on a 16 hr:8 hr light:dark cycle.
source: Adult zebrafish were maintained at 28.5°C on a 16 hr:8 hr light:dark cycle.
evidence: Description of animal husbandry conditions.

claim: All animal work was conducted with approval of the University of California Irvine Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol #AUP-19-043).
source: All animal work in this study was conducted with the approval of the University of California Irvine Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol #AUP-19-043) in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines for the ethical use of animals.
evidence: Statement about ethical approval.

claim: The transgenic embryos Tg(tyrp1b:palmmCherry) were injected with a construct to drive membrane-bound EGFP under the aox5 promoter.
source: The transgenic embryos, Tg(tyrp1b:palmmCherry), were injected with the construct drive membrane-bound EGFP under the aox5 promoter to visualize airinemes in xanthophore lineages and melanophores (Eom et al., 2015).
evidence: Description of experimental methodology with citation.
